questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Nature needed to be different
Within EU
County with good english skills
Good and informative website

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Easy, the webpage was very usefull
There was an into meeting before arrival

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The infocenter handed out the room keys to us renting from the university. 
There were people from the Buddy Programe at the airport. 
The train station, Umeå Östra is very close to the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The student corridor was not "on campus" but it was rented through the university.
You could choose what area you wanted to live in and at what floor. 
Go for Historiegränd - it's right next to ICA in Ålidhem and it's fairly new. Close to IKSU and campus as well.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen in the corridor

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You are in a corridor with 6-10 other people. Make some clear guidelines for cleaning and create a WhatsApp group for communication.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You pre-register with your application to the exchange and then you just have to confirm your seat and your expected participation in the exam before a specific date. This is done on a website called Ladok - very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The teachers and the infocenter

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it within the deadlines. If you don't there is almost nothing they can do and you won't be able to take the exam. Put the dates in your calender.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was more or less the same as you would expect at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more laboratory exercises. Same amount of lectures, but no regular exercises

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Immunology
Bacterial physiology and pathogenesis
Neurobiology
Genetics II

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Immunology - fun if you participate properly and a nice teacher
Bacterial physiology and pathogenesis - fun and interesting
Neurobiology - cool lab exercises
Swedish for Beginners I - easy and good credits - totally doable next to other courses as well

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It's about the same as Denmark. Maybe a bit cheeper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The Buddy Programe is amazing. 
IKSU is 100% worth it!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Buddy Programe. It's a great way to meet new people and to experience Umeå. Do all the things they plan. The moose farm. Icehockey. It only gets better
Go to IKSU as much as you can.
If anyone asks you to pick up their key on the first day - do it! Met my 3 closest exchange friends that way

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes. Stay out late to see the aurora. Go to the city center. Hike around Nydalasjön. Do kayaking on Nydalasjön.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - very close to danish culture. The other exchange students can be a bit more challening though

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You probably won't unless they live in your corridor. Just be nice to them like you would anyone else. Ask if you should have dinner together some nights.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The other exchange students might have a hard time adjusting to speaking english. Just keep doing it yourself. They will come around.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika - afternoon coffee & cake. Do it as much as you can, and get the stampcard for Lindelhallen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
* Prepare your body. Start taking Vitamin D 3-4 months prior to build up enough. Start exercising regularly. Use loiton and oils when it gets below 10*C (at the latest) - the air is super dry.
* If you are going for the fall semester, buy your winther clothes at the Stadium Outlet in Umeå - it's way cheeper. Just bring the essentials (hat, gloves, scarf). 
* If you are going for the fall semester, get a bike as soon as you can. It's much nicer to experience all parts of the city by bike. When the snow comes it will be almost impossible to bike around.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Do everything you want, even if you have to do it alone. 
Go on as many hikes as possible. The whole area is so beautiful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know myself better and people in a similar situation.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not becoming lonely and too homesick

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
